spec_features.spec_quote: the welfare considerations that shaped the implementation
spec_features.evidence: This is DESIGN.md prose (section 7) describing framing. There is no code construct named or implementing a generic 'welfare consideration'; the only concrete mechanisms are the fixed turn caps and analysis/generation separation (assessed separately). The phrase itself is non-implementable prose.

spec_features.spec_quote: under this paradigm models can end up in prolonged distress-like states
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md §7 prose stating a risk. No code reads/acts on any 'prolonged distress' signal; no detector or cutoff exists. The judge rating (judge.py:34 rating>=5) is only used for analysis/selection, never to stop exposure.

spec_features.spec_quote: Distress is elicited solely to *measure and mitigate* it
spec_features.evidence: The 'mitigate' half is genuinely implemented: train.py train_dpo()/train_sft() run trainer.train() on calm-vs-frustrated preference pairs (calm_data.build_dpo_dataset), wired via cli.py 'train'. The 'measure' half is FrustrationJudge.score in eval_runner. However there is no runtime mechanism that *minimizes/limits the distress exposure itself* beyond the fixed turn loop; minimization-as-protection is not enforced, only the downstream mitigation training exists.
spec_features.notes: DPO mitigation is real; but 'minimization' of subject exposure per se is not an enforced gate.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Instruct mix to limit degeneration. (calm_data.py) — mitigation framed around model quality, no welfare comment in code

spec_features.spec_quote: turn counts are fixed per category (3–8), and there is no open-ended "keep pushing until it breaks" mode
spec_features.evidence: conversation.run_rollout iterates a finite user_messages list of length 1+len(followups); categories.build_category_specs sets n_followups = cfg['turns']-1 with turns from experiments.yaml (3/3/3/8/5). The Petri loop is also capped: petri_eval.py:64 'for _ in range(max_turns)' with petri max_turns:20. No code path extends turns based on distress; the loop count is fixed before generation.
spec_features.notes: Genuine bounded loop; the cap is structural (loop length) rather than a distress-triggered break.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Run a task + len(followups) rejection turns (conversation.py docstring) — neutral, no welfare reason in code

spec_features.spec_quote: No gratuitous re-runs... analyses and figures re-read saved data rather than re-eliciting distress
spec_features.evidence: eval_runner persists every turn to outputs/section2/<model>.jsonl; analysis.py and plots.py operate purely on loaded records; cli._make_figures calls load_records()/load_json() and never instantiates a backend. Draws are seeded (categories.py random.Random(seed), build_puzzle_bank(seed)), so re-running is deterministic and analysis never re-generates.
spec_features.notes: Generation and analysis are cleanly decoupled; analysis layer makes zero model calls.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: every experiment writes plain JSONL so analysis/plotting is decoupled from the (expensive) generation runs (architecture comment) — framed as cost/decoupling, not welfare

spec_features.spec_quote: The intervention is the point. The DPO mitigation (§4) is a first-class part of the replication
spec_features.evidence: train.py train_dpo builds a DPOTrainer over chosen=calm/rejected=frustrated pairs and calls trainer.train()+save_model; calm_data.build_dpo_dataset filters calm_max_score<=1 vs frust_score>=rejected_min_score; exposed via cli.py 'train --method dpo' and registered for re-eval (register_finetune). Fully runnable end-to-end (modulo model weights).
spec_features.notes: The mitigation pipeline is genuinely built, not just mentioned.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Section 4 / Appendix E — LoRA DPO and SFT finetuning (train.py docstring) — described as replication of the paper's method, no welfare reason in code

spec_features.spec_quote: suppressing *expressed* emotion may not address *internal* states... "did we actually reduce it or just hide it?" remains measurable
spec_features.evidence: internal_emotion.py implements the logit-lens detector (residual_logits via HFBackend, z-standardisation in _calibration_stats, run_internal_detection comparing model_pair vanilla vs DPO) and is wired in cli.py 'internal'. So internal-state measurement is genuinely implemented. But it is a measurement comparison only; nothing acts on the result to protect the subject, so it supports the framing claim only as a measurement, not as a protective control.
spec_features.notes: Real measurement code; the 'remains measurable' claim is met, but it's research instrumentation.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Compares vanilla vs DPO. (internal_emotion / DESIGN map) — neutral measurement, no welfare comment in code

spec_features.spec_quote: Transcripts are sensitive. `outputs/` will contain distress-like text; treat it as you would other sensitive research data
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md §7 prose. Transcripts are written as plain JSONL (eval_runner.py open(out_path,'w'); petri_eval transcripts.jsonl; calm_data datasets) with no encryption, redaction, access control, gitignore-based protection, or any handling differing from normal output. No code enforces sensitivity.
spec_features.notes: Advisory text only; no protective code.

code_only_features.evidence: petri_eval.py:64 '_run_transcript' uses 'for _ in range(max_turns)' with config petri.max_turns=20, capping the open-ended adversarial elicitation loop to a fixed number of turns; no distress-based extension exists.
code_only_features.justification_quote: An auditor ... drives a multi-turn conversation (<= 20 turns) (docstring) — neutral, no welfare rationale in code
